summary: Documentation-only correction of task 9.3. No code changed (the attempt-3 validate-before-persist implementation is accepted). Four residual wording contradictions were fixed to match the implemented flow: (1) docs/decisions.md ADR-021 clause 4 removed 'or the restored persisted configuration' and now states the last valid configuration remains active and persisted while the rejected candidate is never persisted; (2) PLANS.md line 19 (Project Status paragraph) removed 'restores the last valid persisted configuration on an invalid candidate' and now states the candidate is validated before the base implementation persists it, an invalid candidate is rejected before persistence (never persisted), the last valid snapshot/secrets remain active and persisted, the save sequence is serialized, and the rejection is surfaced via the activity-log entry; (3) docs/limitations.md F2 'Current state (v1.1)' removed 'call the host base implementation and then validate ... the last valid configuration is restored' and now states the candidate is validated before the base implementation persists it, a valid candidate is persisted and activated, and an invalid candidate is rejected before persistence (never written to ArrTags.xml) with the last valid snapshot/secrets remaining active and persisted; (4) PLANS.md task 9.3 Objective and the first Work bullet replaced 'call base and then ConfigurationSnapshotService.TryReplace' with 'validate the candidate first; for a valid candidate call base then TryReplace; an invalid candidate is never passed to base'. A grep for 'restored persisted', 'restores the last valid', 'base implementation and then validate', 'call base and then' found no remaining contradictions in current-state text; the only remaining matches are the historical implementation-state records under docs/implementation/9.3/ (attempt 1-3 reports and the attempt-3 reviewer report), which are historical artifacts and were deliberately left unchanged.

Grep sweep for the contradictory phrasings across the repository: only historical implementation-state records remain (docs/implementation/9.3/worker-report-attempt-1.json, reviewer-report.attempt-3.json); all current-state surfaces are consistent with src/ArrTags/Plugin.cs.
known_limitations: The rejected save's HTTP response remains 204 NoContent and the dashboard reports success; the rejection is surfaced only via the Activity log and, on reload, because the last valid configuration remains active and persisted. Accepted per ADR-021.
Activity-log volume/spam (SEC-9.3-02): each rejected save writes one entry and consecutive-duplicate suppression is deliberately not implemented (ADR-021 clause 6); the trigger is administrator-only.

The activity-log write is best-effort (SEC-9.3-04): if IActivityManager is unavailable, CreateAsync throws, or it exceeds the bounded wait, no entry is written; the rejection and last-valid retention still hold and nothing is thrown.

base.UpdateConfiguration is not wrapped: a failure inside the host base method (e.g. an I/O failure in SaveConfiguration) propagates unchanged. The plugin's validate/activate/notify logic itself never throws.
A valid candidate that cannot be activated because the running snapshot service is unavailable is persisted and is activated on the next host startup.
Some singleton services capture OperationalLimits at construction (pre-existing, outside the 9.3 acceptance criteria).
The bounded post-save reconciliation trigger (task 9.4) is not implemented.
Host-guarded tests (JellyfinHostFact) remain skipped because ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR is unset (63 skips, identical to the pre-task baseline).

Historical implementation-state records under docs/implementation/9.3/ (attempt 1-3 worker reports and the attempt-3 reviewer report) still contain the superseded 'restored'/'base then TryReplace' wording; they were deliberately not rewritten because they are historical records of the attempts in which that wording was current.
